prior_year_events.impact_description: Increased loss ratio for the 2015 YOA driven by the number of lives lost with sums assured above the average; projected to close around break even (adverse for 2015 YOA).

data.standardized_narrative: The gross claims development triangle shows a net favourable movement (release) across older underwriting years (2011-2014) totalling approximately GBP 1.011m released. The syndicate notes an adverse experience in the 2015 underwriting year driven by a number of lives lost with above-average sums assured, although management expect that to normalise. Opening gross claims outstanding (1 Jan 2016) per the balance sheet comparative was GBP 1.113m. The prior-year development figure above was calculated from the gross claims development table in the technical reserves note.
raw_causal_phrases: One of the drivers for the reduced GAAP profit in 2016 was an increased loss ratio for the 2015 YOA, driven by the number of lives lost with the sums assured being above the average.
it is felt that the increased 2015 loss ratio is not representative of how the book should perform in the future and that the loss ratio should normalise at previous levels.
The 2014 underwriting year closed with a profit after all expenses of GBP 1,266k (2013 - a profit of GBP 1,107k), being 12.66% of capacity.
With the increased loss ratio for the 2015 YOA it is projected to close at around a break even position.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (PYD) was not stated explicitly as a gross movement in narrative notes. PYD was calculated from the gross claims development table (claims triangle) for underwriting years 2011-2014 (excluding 2015 & 2016 per methodology). Opening gross claims outstanding was taken from the balance sheet comparative 'Claims outstanding' (2015 column). No explicit sentence describing the total gross prior year movement was found in the notes; exact_reserve_text left empty. No RITC or other distortion was identified in the notes provided.
